req.title: Include Content-Length on echo responses
req.statement: The system shall include a Content-Length header equal to the response body byte length on echo endpoints.

doc.reasoning: The requirement mandates that echo endpoints (/get, /post, /put, /patch, /delete) include a Content-Length header equal to the exact byte length of the response body. Tests must: (1) verify the header is present and numerically exact for each method (positive/EP), (2) verify the header value matches len(response.data) precisely to catch off-by-one mutations (BVA), (3) verify that a body with non-ASCII/multi-byte content still produces a correct Content-Length (boundary), (4) verify that wrong methods return 4xx and do NOT produce a misleading Content-Length on a 2xx body (negative/NEG), and (5) verify the header is present even for an empty-body GET with no query params (BVA zero-length boundary). All tests use Flask test_client() in-process.

tests.name: test_get_content_length_exact_match
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
GET /get endpoint is reachable via test client
actions: Send GET /get with a query parameter
Read response status, Content-Length header, and raw body bytes
expected: Content-Length header value equals str(len(response.data)) exactly
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_get_content_length_exact_match():
    r = client.get('/get?foo=bar')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert 'Content-Length' in r.headers
    cl = int(r.headers['Content-Length'])
    body_len = len(r.data)
    assert cl == body_len, f'Content-Length {cl} != body length {body_len}'
    assert cl > 0

tests.name: test_content_length_not_off_by_one_get
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
GET /get endpoint returns a deterministic body for a fixed request
actions: Send GET /get with no query params
Assert Content-Length == len(body), Content-Length != len(body)-1, Content-Length != len(body)+1
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_content_length_not_off_by_one_get():
    r = client.get('/get')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert 'Content-Length' in r.headers
    cl = int(r.headers['Content-Length'])
    body_len = len(r.data)
    assert cl == body_len
    assert cl != body_len - 1, 'Content-Length is off by -1'
    assert cl != body_len + 1, 'Content-Length is off by +1'

Assert Content-Length equals the byte length of the response body (not character count)

from httpbin.core import app
import json
client = app.test_client()

def test_content_length_with_multibyte_unicode_body():

    r = client.post('/post', data=payload, content_type='application/json')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert 'Content-Length' in r.headers
    cl = int(r.headers['Content-Length'])
    body_bytes = r.data
    body_len = len(body_bytes)
    assert cl == body_len, f'Content-Length {cl} != byte length {body_len}'
    assert cl >= body_len

tests.name: test_content_length_header_is_integer_string
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
All five echo endpoints are reachable
actions: Send requests to all five echo endpoints
For each, assert Content-Length is a valid integer string and equals body byte length
expected: All five have Content-Length header parseable as integer
All five Content-Length values equal len(response.data)
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_content_length_header_is_integer_string():
    responses = [
        client.get('/get'),
        client.post('/post'),
        client.put('/put'),
        client.patch('/patch'),
        client.delete('/delete'),
    ]
    for r in responses:
        assert r.status_code == 200
        assert 'Content-Length' in r.headers
        cl_str = r.headers['Content-Length']
        cl = int(cl_str)
        assert cl == len(r.data)
        assert cl > 0

tests.name: test_content_length_changes_with_larger_body
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
POST /post echoes the JSON body in the response
actions: Send POST /post with a small body, record Content-Length
Send POST /post with a larger body, record Content-Length
Assert both equal their respective body byte lengths
expected: Content-Length for larger body > Content-Length for smaller body
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
import json
client = app.test_client()

def test_content_length_changes_with_larger_body():
    small = json.dumps({'a': '1'})
    large = json.dumps({'a': 'x' * 500})
    r1 = client.post('/post', data=small, content_type='application/json')
    r2 = client.post('/post', data=large, content_type='application/json')
    assert r1.status_code == 200
    assert r2.status_code == 200
    cl1 = int(r1.headers['Content-Length'])
    cl2 = int(r2.headers['Content-Length'])
    assert cl1 == len(r1.data)
    assert cl2 == len(r2.data)
    assert cl2 > cl1

tests.name: test_content_length_consistent_across_identical_requests
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
GET /get is deterministic for identical requests
actions: Send GET /get twice with identical parameters
Assert both Content-Length values are equal and match body lengths
expected: Both Content-Length values equal their respective body byte lengths
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_content_length_consistent_across_identical_requests():
    r1 = client.get('/get?stable=1')
    r2 = client.get('/get?stable=1')
    assert r1.status_code == 200
    assert r2.status_code == 200
    cl1 = int(r1.headers['Content-Length'])
    cl2 = int(r2.headers['Content-Length'])
    assert cl1 == len(r1.data)
    assert cl2 == len(r2.data)
    assert cl1 == cl2
